findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type, colliding between anonymous:0 and render:0
findings.body: `validateSubject` parses `req.GetSubject()` with `types.ParseTypeID`, which sets `checkReq.UserUID` to `"0"` for both `anonymous:0` (`types.TypeAnonymous`) and `render:0` (`types.TypeRenderService`). Because `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses only `checkReq.UserUID` and does not include `checkReq.IdentityType` (or the full subject), when `anonymous:0` is denied `dashboards:read`, `folders:read`, or `datasources:read` on a resource, `permDenialCache` stores the denial under `<namespace>.perm_0_<action>_<name>_<parent>`. Any subsequent `Check` from `render:0` for the same resource within `shortCacheTTL` (30s) will hit that denial cache entry and return `Allowed: false`, breaking dashboard rendering even though `TypeRenderService` has wildcard read permissions. Additionally, for user subjects specified by numeric ID versus UID, `permDenialCache` keys on the raw `checkReq.UserUID` while `permCache` normalizes via `GetUserIdentifiers`.

findings.title: Check and List execute duplicate DB lookup when GetUserIdentifiers fails
findings.body: `getCachedIdentityPermissions` calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers(ctx, ns, userID)`, which queries the database when `idCache` misses. If `GetUserIdentifiers` returns an error (for example, if the user does not exist or the database query fails), `Check` (line 124) and `List` (line 180) treat any non-nil error as a cache miss and immediately invoke `s.getIdentityPermissions`, which calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers` a second time and repeats the failing database query. Callers should return early when `err != nil && !errors.Is(err, cache.ErrNotFound)` (or `getCachedIdentityPermissions` should only read from `idCache`).

findings.title: Denial cache test sets cached permission to false instead of true
findings.body: In `TestService_CacheCheck` ("Should deny on explicit cache deny entry"), line 982 sets `s.permCache` with `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}` even though the comment above it says `// Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked`. Because the scope value is `false` and the fake store has no permissions, `s.Check` would return `Allowed: false` even if `permDenialCache` were completely ignored. The value in `permCache` should be `true` to verify that `permDenialCache` short-circuits `permCache`.
